rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 6 compounds within the run if possible and map the overall elution window. This should reveal whether retention is compressed, whether any compounds are near-unretained or too late, and where to focus later optimization.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the objective is now to cut analysis time while keeping every peak inside the gradient. The first and last peaks correspond to roughly phi_e ≈ 0.18 and 0.68 in the scout, so a narrower, steeper window with higher temperature should pull the run closer to 10 minutes and test how much time can be removed before resolution starts to suffer.

We already have full resolution and are just 0.52 min over the 10 min target, so the next move is a modest shortening at the same window and temperature. This directly tests whether we can bring the last peak under 10 min while preserving the current limiting pair resolution, especially peaks 1 and 2.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so now the goal is to find the fastest method that still keeps every adjacent pair at R >= 1.5. Reducing tG one more step at the same window and temperature is the cleanest way to probe the resolution limit, with the early 1/2 pair still expected to be the critical one.

The 6 min method still has comfortable margin on the limiting 1/2 pair, so push the gradient steeper again to locate the shortest fully resolved method. Keeping phi0, phi1, and T fixed isolates the effect of slope and should show whether we can gain more speed before the first pair drops below R = 1.5.

At 4 min the limiting 1/2 pair is still just above full-credit resolution, so one final reduction in tG will test the shortest possible gradient on the grid. This should establish whether 2 min is still fully resolved or whether 4 min is the practical lower bound.

Since the 2 min run failed only on the first pair and that pair elutes very early, lowering phi0 should selectively retain and spread peaks 1 and 2 with minimal penalty to the rest. Keeping tG at 4 min preserves the very short runtime while testing whether extra low-organic focusing can increase the critical early resolution.

Lowering phi0 at 4 min improved the critical 1/2 pair substantially, so the obvious next test is whether that gain is enough to rescue the 2 min gradient. This directly probes whether we can beat the current fastest fully resolved method while keeping the late peaks well within the run.

The 2 min gradients remain limited by the first pair, and lowering phi0 from 0.20 to 0.15 helped that pair at 4 min, so push phi0 one more step lower while keeping the successful 4 min format. This tests whether stronger early retention can create enough margin on peaks 1/2 to support a later attempt at an even faster method.

The lower phi0 again improved the critical 1/2 pair at 4 min, so the next step is to see whether that added margin is finally enough to make the 2 min gradient fully resolved. This is the most direct test of whether we can shorten the method below the current 4 min optimum without changing the rest of the selectivity pattern.

The first pair clearly depends on the low-end composition, so take phi0 to the minimum while keeping the proven 4 min format to maximize early retention and see whether the critical pair can be widened further. If this improves R(1,2) again, it will show whether there is any remaining path toward a shorter fully resolved method.

The 4 min method is robustly fully resolved, and varying phi0 showed the first pair is highly composition-sensitive with a maximum near 0.10–0.15 rather than monotonically improving at lower phi0. Testing a higher phi0 at the same 4 min slope helps map that selectivity surface and may reveal whether we can trade some early resolution to shorten or sharpen the overall separation differently.

Since all compounds elute well before the end of the current 0.65 window, trimming phi1 slightly should reduce the effective gradient range and may improve the critical low-end selectivity while keeping the run very short. Using phi0 = 0.15 preserves one of the best early-pair conditions seen so far at 4 min.

Narrowing the gradient to phi1 = 0.60 improved the critical 1/2 pair at 4 min, so the key question is whether that added selectivity is enough to make the 2 min method fully resolved. This is the most promising remaining route to a faster optimum because all later pairs still have ample margin.

The 2 min run improved when phi1 was lowered from 0.65 to 0.60, and the last peak still remains comfortably early, so trimming the upper end again is the best chance to squeeze more early-pair selectivity out of the same very short gradient. This directly tests whether a narrower 0.15–0.55 window can push the 1/2 pair to full resolution without sacrificing elution of the late compound.

The 2 min method keeps improving as the window narrows on the high-organic end, and the last peak is still under 10 min, so one more reduction in phi1 is justified. This is the best remaining direct test of whether a sufficiently narrow 2 min window can finally bring the critical 1/2 pair to R >= 1.5 while keeping all six compounds observed.

At 2 min and phi1 = 0.55 the only shortfall is the early 1/2 pair, while the last peak is still comfortably before 10 min, so temperature is the remaining lever to adjust selectivity without changing the basic fast window. A 5 C increase may reorder or modestly spread that close pair while also offsetting some of the late retention risk if we stay near this narrow gradient range.

Raising temperature worsened the critical 1/2 pair, so test the opposite direction at the same promising 2 min, 0.15–0.55 window. Lower temperature is the remaining clean way to probe whether selectivity for that pair can improve enough to approach full resolution while still keeping the last peak under 10 minutes.

The 2 min, 0.15–0.55, 45 C run is essentially at full resolution, so the next useful step is to see whether higher temperature can cut cycle time in a still-robust 4 min method without losing full credit. This probes whether a hotter version of the already optimal 4 min strategy can match the current best CRF while giving a faster practical method than the existing 4 min runs.

The best 2 min result came from cooler temperature and a narrowed upper window, while 4 min methods remain fully resolved with room to explore a slightly higher phi0. This run tests whether shifting the whole 4 min window upward at 45 C can keep the critical pair above 1.5 while reducing the retention penalty of the narrowed phi1 approach, potentially giving a faster fully resolved practical optimum.

This window at 4 min and 45 C gives unusually strong margin on the critical 1/2 pair, so it is the best candidate to revisit a 2 min gradient. If any 2 min method can reach full resolution, this combination should have the highest chance while still keeping the last peak under 10 min.

The 0.20–0.60, 2 min, 45 C run came closest so far among the truly fast methods, missing only on the first pair. Narrowing phi1 one step should further flatten the gradient and may give the extra early-pair resolution needed, while the last peak still has room to remain under 10 minutes.

Now that 0.20–0.55 at 2 min and 45 C reaches full resolution, a small upward shift of the whole window is the most direct way to test whether we can shorten retention further while staying above the 1.5 threshold for the critical first pair. With only a narrow safety margin on peaks 1/2, this is an efficient boundary test around the new fast optimum.

We now know the best fast method is right at the boundary, and lowering phi1 from 0.60 to 0.55 rescued the 2 min run at phi0 = 0.20. Testing phi1 = 0.50 at the same phi0 and temperature checks whether the window can be narrowed one more step to retain full resolution while potentially defining the lower edge of the feasible 2 min operating space.

The current best fast method is 0.20–0.55, 2 min, 45 C with the critical pair only just above threshold, so the last remaining worthwhile test is a slightly lower temperature at the same window. Cooling may further improve selectivity for peaks 1/2 while still keeping the last peak below 10 min, potentially giving a more robust fastest fully resolved method.
